newsitem.title: USA: U.S Northwest spot power prices continue to drop.
newsitem.headline: U.S Northwest spot power prices continue to drop.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Northwest fell further amid mild temperatures and ample hydropower supplies, while Southwest prices were largely steady, market sources said Tuesday.
"The weather is warmer and there is a lot more water," said a Portland, Oregon, trader.

Bonneville Power Administration (BPA), the federal agency which markets power produced at U.S. dams in the Pacific Northwest, on Tuesday began offering next-day surplus power during peak as well as off-peak hours for the first time in almost two weeks.
BPA offered up to 200 MW of firm on-peak power in the Northwest at $22.25 per megawatt hour, compared with $32.00 for late November offers.
But trade sources in the region said some other sellers were able to undercut BPA's prices.
Firm, peak California-Oregon border (COB) electricity for Wednesday was assessed at $22.00-23.25 per megawatt hour (MWH), down from $24.00-25.00 for Tuesday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Wednesday was little changed at $15.00-16.00.
Wednesday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was down at $20.00-21.00, while off-peak was fairly steady at $14.00-16.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Wednesday was quoted at $22.00-23.00 per MWh, little changed from Tuesday's pre-schedulings. Firm, off-peak PV power was quoted at $14.00-15.00.
Wednesday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were also steady at $22.00-24.00 per MWh, while firm off-peak was assessed at $14.00-16.00.
